# GitHub Copilot Instructions for Barber

## Project Overview
This is a Barber repository for managing barbershop operations. When contributing to this project, follow these guidelines to ensure consistency and quality.

## Code Style and Standards

### General Principles
- Write clean, maintainable, and well-documented code
- Follow the existing code style and conventions in the repository
- Keep functions small and focused on a single responsibility
- Use meaningful variable and function names that clearly indicate their purpose

### Comments and Documentation
- Add comments for complex logic or non-obvious implementations
- Keep comments up-to-date with code changes
- Document public APIs and interfaces
- Use inline comments sparingly and only when necessary to explain "why" rather than "what"

## Development Workflow

### Before Making Changes
1. Understand the existing codebase structure
2. Check for similar implementations or patterns in the repository
3. Consider the impact of changes on existing functionality
4. Review related tests before making modifications

### Testing
- Write tests for new features and bug fixes
- Ensure all existing tests pass before submitting changes
- Follow the existing test structure and naming conventions
- Include both positive and negative test cases

### Version Control
- Make small, focused commits with clear messages
- Keep changes minimal and targeted to the specific issue
- Avoid mixing refactoring with feature changes
- Review your own changes before committing

## Best Practices

### Code Quality
- Avoid code duplication - reuse existing functions when possible
- Handle errors gracefully and provide meaningful error messages
- Validate inputs and handle edge cases
- Follow security best practices (no hardcoded credentials, sanitize inputs, etc.)

### Performance
- Consider performance implications of your changes
- Avoid unnecessary computations or database queries
- Use appropriate data structures for the task at hand

### Maintainability
- Keep dependencies up to date
- Remove unused code and dependencies
- Refactor when you see opportunities for improvement
- Document architectural decisions

## Specific Guidelines for This Repository

### File Organization
- Follow the existing directory structure
- Place related files together logically
- Keep configuration files in appropriate locations

### Naming Conventions
- Use consistent naming patterns across the codebase
- Follow language-specific naming conventions
- Make names descriptive but not overly verbose

## When Using Copilot

### Do:
- Review and understand generated code before accepting
- Verify that suggested code follows project conventions
- Test generated code thoroughly
- Adapt suggestions to fit the project's specific needs

### Don't:
- Blindly accept all suggestions without review
- Commit code that you don't understand
- Ignore existing patterns in favor of generated alternatives
- Skip testing generated code

## Questions or Issues?
If you're unsure about any aspect of development, review existing similar code in the repository for guidance, or consult with the project maintainers.
